summary: Ordu-Giresun Airport is a medium-sized regional airport serving two provinces on Turkey's Black Sea coast, Ordu and Giresun. Its most distinctive feature is that the runway was constructed on a man-made island extending into the Black Sea, making it one of the only airports in Turkey—and among a handful worldwide—built largely over water to overcome the region's mountainous terrain. Opened in 2015, it replaced earlier limited air service and now handles domestic flights year-round with occasional seasonal international routes.
faqs:
Q: Why is Ordu-Giresun Airport built on a man-made island in the sea?
A: The Turkish Black Sea coast is dominated by steep coastal mountains, leaving no suitable flat land for a long runway. Engineers extended the facility into the sea on reclaimed land to provide a safe approach and adequate runway length.

Q: When did the airport begin operations?
A: The airport officially opened in 2015, taking over passenger flights from smaller airfields that had previously served the region.

Q: Which airlines fly from Ordu-Giresun Airport?
A: Turkish Airlines operates the majority of scheduled domestic flights, primarily connecting Ordu and Giresun with Istanbul
